P-999.exposure_contrast: Any antihypertensive medication (ATC C02, C03, C07, C08, C09, combinations included) consumed during the study period vs no antihypertensive medication of any class; not modelled as time-varying.
P-999.population: 128,683 US Optum CDM claimants (2007 to Oct 2020) with 12 or more months of enrolment and at least one year of prescription records before a first MCI diagnosis and no prior ADRD, restricted by design to hypertensive patients (the hypertension ICD codes printed on p.8 are COPD codes, evidently a transcription error); mean age at MCI 75.5 (users) and 78.0 (non-users).
P-999.outcome: Incident ADRD by ICD-9/10 codes (AD, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal, non-specific) or the second of two anti-dementia (ATC N06D) pharmacy claims within any 6 months.
P-999.horizon: First MCI diagnosis to ADRD or last healthcare encounter; no fixed horizon; mean 21.96 to 22.87 months to ADRD among converters (Table 1).
P-999.adjustment_set: Age (6 bands), sex, race, 13 comorbidities (AF, CHF, COPD, hyperlipidemia, IHD, obesity, TBI, T2DM, stroke, anxiety, depression, substance use, tobacco), statin and metformin use; hypertension held constant by restriction.
P-999.result: aHR 1.06 (1.04-1.08); 0.84 (0.80-0.88) among statin users and 1.11 (1.08-1.13) among statin non-users (interaction P < 0.001).

P-1157.exposure_contrast: Baseline prescription in the pooled 'Antihypertensive Drugs' category (Figure 3 has no separate class rows) vs no such prescription.
P-1157.population: 237 Taiwanese veterans aged over 60 at CDR 0.5 (Veterans Home residents enrolled 2017-2018, Kaohsiung VGH geriatric/neurology outpatients 2019-2023); mean age about 78.7; 154 of 237 (65%) hypertensive, so at least 83 participants had no hypertension.
P-1157.outcome: CDR 0.5 to 1 at annual in-person assessment, confirmed by neurologists (ICD-10/ICD-11); all-cause (57 AD, 14 vascular, 15 mixed, 2 DLB, 1 FTD).
P-1157.adjustment_set: Age, sex, CCI, education, smoking, hearing and visual impairment, Barthel, GDS-15, MNA-SF, recruitment source; no hypertension term and no co-medication term.

estimand_side_by_side.waivable_gate_mismatches: Dataset family (Optum claims vs Kaohsiung veterans cohort), outcome ascertainment (claims codes or anti-dementia fills vs neurologist-confirmed CDR 1) and horizon (both roughly 2 to 3 years): each could reasonably be waived for two independent pharmacoepidemiologic cohorts on the same all-cause dementia endpoint.
estimand_side_by_side.different_estimand: The comparator. P-999's non-users are untreated hypertensives; P-1157's non-users are mostly normotensive. Because the restriction variable is the exposure's indication, the same label ('antihypertensive use vs non-use') denotes a different comparison in each study. Co-medication conditioning is a second difference: P-999's estimate reverses sign with statin use and P-1157 conditions on no co-medication.

strongest_case_against_the_verdict: P-1157's Figure 3 shows 'Antihypertensive Drugs' as one pooled category, so its HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93) carries the same label as P-999's any-AHM-vs-none aHR 1.06 (1.04-1.08): antihypertensive use vs non-use in older adults with MCI, all-cause dementia, adjusted Cox HR. The directions are opposite, each interval excludes 1 and the intervals are disjoint, which meets the brief's reading of 'incompatible'. Task (T2), validation tier (n/a: two association studies) and modality family (medication-exposure records) match. The dataset-family mismatch is what independent replication looks like, and a cohort difference was waived before (C-232). On this reading, P-999's restriction to hypertensives is a narrower sample of the same population class: 65% of P-1157 is hypertensive and its antihypertensive users are predominantly hypertensive. P-1157's missing hypertension covariate would then be a confounding weakness in P-1157, a reason to doubt one estimate rather than a reason to call them different quantities. Treating every difference in adjustment set as a different quantity would make no two observational studies comparable, which is exactly the external critic's objection.
why_it_does_or_does_not_succeed: The case fails on the comparison, not on the gate. P-999 restricts on the exposure's own indication, so 'non-user' denotes a different clinical state in each study: an untreated hypertensive in P-999 (28,005 of 128,683), and mostly a participant without hypertension in P-1157 (at least 83 of 237, with no hypertension term in the model). P-999's authors restricted the cohort for exactly this reason: including normotensives 'would add a potential confounder (hypertension status) that could not be well controlled as very few normotensive patients are taking AHMs'. P-1157's own counts show why this matters. From Table 2, 47 of 154 hypertensive participants progressed (30.5%) against 42 of 83 without hypertension (50.6%), a crude ratio of about 0.60, the same size as the adjusted antihypertensive HR of 0.59. Nothing in P-1157 separates the two associations. Both reported results can therefore hold at once: hypertension status goes with slower progression in the Kaohsiung cohort, while treated and untreated hypertensives in Optum differ little. The pair passes the incompatibility test only if the two quantities are treated as one, and they are not one. Co-medication is a second difference. P-999's estimate for the same labelled contrast is 0.84 (0.80-0.88) with statins and 1.11 (1.08-1.13) without. P-1157 conditions on no co-medication, although its lipid-modifying agents carry HR 0.43, and its interval contains P-999's statin-user estimate, so on one plausible alignment the numbers are even compatible. This is not a confounding critique relabelled: the reference category is a different population, and two studies sharing that population and comparator could still contradict each other. The first reader's dataset-family ground is the weakest of their five; a waiver would be reasonable here, and the verdict does not need that ground. A waiver still cannot cure a comparator difference (the C-232/C-80 reasoning). I checked all ten first-reader quotes on their cited pages (all verbatim) and every number in their file against the PDFs, and found no factual error. I also checked P-999's stratum labels. The Table 5 footnote and Figure 1 give the statin-user stratum as N = 59,980, whereas Table 1 gives 68,703 statin users. The interval widths fit Table 1's strata (0.80-0.88 rests on only 3,029 statin-using non-users), so the labels are swapped, not the estimates, and the first reader's reading of 0.84 as the statin-user figure stands. No corpus study bridges the pair on a common quantity: P-1002 reports average treatment effects, not hazard ratios, in an unrestricted EHR cohort.
grounds: Exposure contrast: P-999 compares hypertensive MCI patients who consumed any antihypertensive during the study period with hypertensive MCI patients who took none; P-1157 compares MCI participants with a baseline prescription in its pooled 'Antihypertensive Drugs' category against participants without one, most of whom have no hypertension.

Population: P-999 is 128,683 US claimants restricted by design to hypertension, with a first MCI diagnosis at a mean age of about 76; P-1157 is 237 Taiwanese veterans aged over 60 at CDR 0.5, 65% (154/237) of them hypertensive.

Outcome and horizon: P-999 counts claims-coded ADRD or a second anti-dementia fill, followed to the last encounter (mean about 22 months to ADRD among converters); P-1157 counts neurologist-confirmed CDR 1 at annual visits over a median 34 months; both are all-cause dementia, and this difference alone would be tolerable.

Adjustment set: P-999 adjusts for age, sex, race, 13 comorbidities and statin and metformin use, and holds hypertension constant by restriction; P-1157 adjusts for age, sex, CCI, education, smoking, sensory impairment, Barthel, GDS-15, MNA-SF and recruitment source, with no hypertension or co-medication term.

The dataset-family, ascertainment and horizon mismatches are gate-level differences that could reasonably be waived for two independent pharmacoepidemiologic cohorts, so the verdict does not rest on them.

The comparator is not waivable: it differs in kind (untreated hypertensives vs mostly normotensives), and P-999's authors name this as the reason they excluded normotensives, so the two HRs are different estimands, not two estimates of one estimand separated by a gate.

P-1157's hypertension-status association (30.5% vs 50.6% progression, crude ratio about 0.60, derived from Table 2) is the size of its antihypertensive HR (0.59), so its estimate cannot be separated from hypertension status and both papers' results can be true together.

P-999's estimate for the same labelled contrast runs from 0.84 (0.80-0.88) with statins to 1.11 (1.08-1.13) without, and P-1157's interval contains the former, so without a co-medication-matched P-1157 estimate no pairing is incompatible on a common quantity.

The record's own framing (class-level 0.96-0.98 against a medication-count HR of 0.49) sets different exposures against each other, as the first reader found, so the verdict holds on every alignment of the two papers' estimates.
